generated.title: Japan 2011: Magnitude 9.1 and the Tohoku Tsunami
generated.description:
On March 11, 2011, a magnitude 9.1 earthquake struck off the northeast coast of Japan.

Here, the Pacific plate dives beneath northern Japan. The plates had been locked, storing strain, until the fault slipped by tens of meters beneath the seafloor. The seafloor was thrust upward and a tsunami struck the coast, surging more than thirty meters up the land in places. More than fifteen thousand people lost their lives. The tsunami also crippled the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant, forcing evacuations. Japan later reworked its warnings, after early alerts underestimated the tsunami.

The lesson: near the coast, strong shaking is itself the warning.
